newsitem.title: UK: London gold ticks higher on short covering.
newsitem.headline: London gold ticks higher on short covering.

text.p: Gold prices edged higher on modest short covering early on Wednesday and further gains may be possible in the near term, dealers said.
But they said gold was eventually likely to retest recent lows and then drop further.
Explaining the bounce in the price from an 18-month low struck on Tuesday, one dealer said: "It's been too bearish to be true recently and when everyone's bearish, it tends to go the other way."
Gold fixed firmer at $379.20 an ounce in the morning, compared with an 18-month low fix of $377.05 on Tuesday morning and $378.65 in the afternoon.
Getting back above the key $380 level was certain to be a problem for gold, after it attracted some buying support around $377 on Tuesday when the market was short, dealers said.
"There's a little bit of short covering this morning but I don't know how long-lived that's going to be," a dealer said.
Strength in the dollar and booming U.S. stock and bond markets are discouraging investor interest, while physical demand is on hold until prices bottom out, analysts said.
Poor Asian demand and the prospect of producer forward selling and central bank sales all pointed to a bear trend, said metals analyst Ted Arnold of broker Merrill Lynch.

"By the middle of September sentiment was clearly beginning to turn bearish and now I suspect it is only a matter of weeks before we see the $370 basis spot support level decisively broken on the downside," Arnold said.
After prices hit $370, an attempt towards $350 could not be ruled out, Arnold added.
Silver was barely changed at $4.92, up one cent.
Prices had firmed from the high $4.80s on Tuesday afternoon on a shortcovering rally. But dealers said gains toward the key $5.00 resistance level would be hard won.
"Silver has been having lots of problems closing above $4.92. There's a lot of resistance below $5.00," one said.
Platinum was steady, just $0.25 under the Tuesday London close, at $384.00. On the upside it targeted $385.
Palladium, however, probed its important $120 resistance level for the first time since it cracked over a week ago. Prices hit three-year lows last month.
